original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Quotient the BIT local word's eight-axis ambient by the linear map phi(x) = drop_j(x xor v) with kernel span{v}, for v = 150 chosen from the 255 directions by scan_kernels.py (all 255 replay; 150 best), then re-pad the full-ambient frame so every helper remains physically D_I8 and the tensor block stays 7. This moves the BIT supplier from 0.003464248972 to 0.012401086416; with the complex supplier at 0.015637149091 the outer min(complex, BIT) becomes 0.012401 (+310.6% over 0.00302015).
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a replacement H2/K interface. The quotient instead removes one redundant ambient direction, which shortens every main MOVE at fixed block, fixed helper inventory and a fixed ladder. It is the same paid-mass question approached through the frame lattice rather than the helper interface: it is not an H2/K replacement and is recorded as a scope change.
bottleneck_link: The BIT supplier binds the outer kappa whenever the complex supplier sits above it. The local paid rank mass is the term the ambient frame lattice controls directly, and a one-dimensional quotient removes one rank from every MOVE whose destination contains the kernel while leaving the ladder and the helpers untouched.
stop_rule: Stop when the quotient word fails the shipped local record interpreter on any endpoint, any arbitrary input column, the ADD/COPY counts or the helper D_I8 contract, or fails to improve the two-constraint screen over the emitted word.
evidence: BIT supplier kappa 0.003464248972 -> 0.012401086416 (+258.0%); outer min(complex, BIT) 0.00302015 -> 0.012401 (+310.6%). verify.py replays the pinned source word (reproducing the declared local bill {1:1323,2:1342,3:79,4:44,5:102,6:11,7:19}) and the quotient in both directions: 24,305 ADDs, 9 COPY episodes, all 661 endpoints and all arbitrary input columns exact, paid profiles identical, helper starts at ground and finals at dim 8, ambient dim 8. scan_kernels.py builds, replays and prices all 255 directions.
author: Douglas Colkitt, with substantial AI assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for derivation, implementation, checking and writing; no independent human or formal-kernel review claimed.
